title: Revenue by region report
summary: Group orders by region into a sorted summary, counting only paid orders from messy input.
prompt: Finance wants a revenue summary per region. Write `summarize(orders: Order[]): RegionSummary[]` with these
interface Order { region: string; amountCents: number; status: "paid" | "refunded" | "pending" }
interface RegionSummary { region: string; orders: number; revenueCents: number; averageCents: number }
- Count only `"paid"` orders. Regions with no paid orders are left out.
- Region labels are typed by hand: trim them and uppercase them (`" eu "` and `"EU"` are the same region, reported as `"EU"`).
- Sort by `revenueCents` descending; **equal revenue is ordered by region name**, A to Z.
solution: const totals = new Map<string, { orders: number; revenueCents: number }>();
.map(([region, t]) => ({ region, orders: t.orders, revenueCents: t.revenueCents, averageCents: Math.round(t.revenueCents / t.orders) }))
.sort((a, b) => b.revenueCents - a.revenueCents || (a.region < b.region ? -1 : a.region > b.region ? 1 : 0));
template: interface Order { region: string; amountCents: number; status: "paid" | "refunded" | "pending" }
interface RegionSummary { region: string; orders: number; revenueCents: number; averageCents: number }
Dojo.eq("regions in order: revenue high to low, ties A to Z", ["APAC", "US", "EU"], dojoReport.map(r => r.region));
Dojo.eq("EU: three paid orders from three spellings", { region: "EU", orders: 3, revenueCents: 4999, averageCents: 1666 }, dojoReport.find(r => r.region === "EU"));
Dojo.eq("US: the pending order is not counted", { region: "US", orders: 1, revenueCents: 5000, averageCents: 5000 }, dojoReport.find(r => r.region === "US"));
Dojo.eq("APAC", { region: "APAC", orders: 2, revenueCents: 5000, averageCents: 2500 }, dojoReport.find(r => r.region === "APAC"));
Dojo.check("LATAM (only refunds) is left out", !dojoReport.some(r => r.region === "LATAM"), "LATAM had no paid orders");
